title: Meet ψ
intro: This glow is one particle. Press Play, watch the green ring, and press Observe while it is high.
goal: Press Play, then Observe while the green ring is high.
naiveSkip: tutorial: the launch is fixed, the level teaches the controls

tutorial.title: Meet ψ
tutorial.text: This glow is the wavefunction ψ of one particle. Brightness shows |ψ|, colour shows its phase (the wheel in the corner).
tutorial.phys: There is no hidden dot inside. Until someone looks, ψ is the whole description of the particle.

tutorial.title: Let it evolve
tutorial.text: Press Play. Nobody pushes the packet: the Schrödinger equation alone moves it and spreads it out.
tutorial.phys: The colour bands are the phase. Their spacing is the wavelength λ = 2π/k₀ = 3.5, and they march in the direction of travel.

tutorial.title: Read the odds
tutorial.text: The green ring is P<sub>T</sub>: the probability of finding the particle in the green circle if you looked right now. The timeline under the field records it.
tutorial.phys: P<sub>T</sub> is |ψ|² added up over the target. That is the Born rule.

tutorial.title: Look
tutorial.text: Press Observe now, while the ring is high. The particle will be found at one spot, picked at random with probability |ψ|².
tutorial.phys: Looking changes ψ: right after the measurement it is a small blob where the particle was found.

tutorial.title: Chance and skill
tutorial.text: Hit or miss is chance. Stars come from P<sub>T</sub> at the moment you looked, so they rate your play, not your luck. A miss scores nothing: Retry rolls new dice.

physics.point: A particle is described by a wave ψ. Where you will find it is random, with probability |ψ|²: the Born rule.

idea: In quantum mechanics a particle has no definite position until it is measured. What it does have is a wavefunction ψ, a complex number at every point of space that evolves smoothly and predictably by the Schrödinger equation.

When you measure the position, you get one definite answer. Which one is random. The probability of finding the particle in a region is the integral of |ψ|² over that region. Max Born proposed this in 1926, and it is the only rule of this game.
The colours show the phase of ψ, the part |ψ|² throws away. You cannot see phase in a single measurement, but it decides where waves add up and where they cancel, as later chapters show.
maths: The packet starts as a Gaussian with width σ₀ = 1.6 and wavenumber k₀ = 1.8 (units ħ = m = 1):

maths.eq: ψ(x, y, 0) ∝ exp(−|r − r₀|² / 4σ₀²) · exp(i k₀ x)

maths: It evolves by the free Schrödinger equation iħ ∂ψ/∂t = −(ħ²/2m)∇²ψ. Its centre moves at the group velocity k₀ = 1.8, so it covers the 19 units to the target centre in about t = 10.6. The meter peaks a little earlier, at t ≈ 10 (62%), because the spreading packet starts filling the circle before its centre arrives.
The meter shows P<sub>T</sub> = ∫<sub>T</sub> |ψ|² d²x. Observe draws one point from |ψ|²; the chance that it lands in the target is exactly P<sub>T</sub>.
try: Observe very early (t ≈ 3). P<sub>T</sub> is near zero, so you will almost always miss.
Observe at the peak several times. You will hit in roughly 6 runs out of 10, and miss in the rest, with the same ψ every time.
Switch the view to |ψ|² to see only the probability density, without the phase colours.
